item.description: Caitlin Clark of the Indiana Fever, WNBA MVP A'ja Wilson of the Las Vegas Aces and 2026 Rookie of the Year Olivia Miles of the Minnesota Lynx earned 2026 All-WNBA First Team selections, which the league announced ahead of Saturday's Game 3 of the WNBA Finals . Miles was the only first-timer among the First Team this season, while Clark and Fever teammate Kelsey Mitchell were named for the second time each. New York Liberty star Breanna Stewart was a First Team choice for the seventh time in her career. item.title: “It has to be done”: Michael Carrick fires demand to his Man United stars ahead of Bournemouth
item.description: “It has to be done”: Michael Carrick fires demand to his Man United stars ahead of Bournemouth Manchester United boss Michael Carrick has made a demand of his players ahead of Sunday’s home meeting with Bournemouth. Must-win game The game against Bournemouth feels like the biggest of Carrick’s managerial career so far, given the uncertainties surrounding his position. Carrick is under immense pressure due to United’s miserable start to the season. United are languishing in the bottom half of the Premier League table, having managed just seven points from as many opening games. Wednesday’s 4-1 hammering at the hands of Como has sparked a fresh wave of criticism directed at Carrick, which was not made any easier by Bruno Fernandes questioning his tactical decisions after the final whistle. United are believed to be doing their groundwork in the event they need to pull the trigger and sack Carrick imminently. Potential replacements for the legendary midfielder include Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann, Antonio Conte, Fabian Hurzeler and Unai Emery. Carrick spoke to MUTV and demanded that his player deliver a much-improved performance when the Cherries make their way to Old Trafford. Carrick’s demand The 45-year-old said, “It has to be done. The motivation and the inspiration is there, you’ve got to feel that drive.” “We were all bitterly disappointed with a lot of things in the game [at Como] – the result, the performance.” “We’ve got a chance to put that in a different direction. We’ll never replace it, never get it back but we can make the difference in the next game now and we have to.” Carrick added, “We just want to look like ourselves, be the best version of us. We know we can be a lot better than what we were during the week.” “We are more than capable of winning football matches and we want to put the things in place to allow us to do that.” He said about Bournemouth, “They’re a very good team. I’m really impressed with them, I have to say. They are very intense and do a lot of things very, very well. They have been unfortunate with some of their results, they should have a bit more from the games, in terms of points, and I’m fully aware of what type of game it’s going to be on Sunday.” “We have to be fully ready.” The contest kicks off at 3 pm. Featured image by Molly Darlington/Getty Images

item.title: Spurs boss Ho wants 'more support and training' for WSL referees
item.description: Tottenham manager Martin Ho says Women's Super League referees "need more support" as he vented his frustration over a controversial penalty decision in their derby defeat by Arsenal. A 2-1 win for the Gunners at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Saturday was settled by Alessia Russo's spot-kick in the 56th minute. Referee Phoebe Cross awarded the decision after Lisa Baum's shot bounced off the post and Cathinka Tandberg's clearance hit Spurs team-mate Ella Morris' outstretched hand. According to the laws, if the ball hits a hand after it was played by a team-mate, an indirect free-kick should be awarded. Ho said: "My interpretation of the rule is if your team-mate hits it and your team-mate is one yard away, time and distance is taken into account and it's not a penalty. "That's what we were told at the start of the season in the referee's meeting. I asked the question, 'how is it [a penalty] from that distance?' They couldn't give me an answer on the pitch. "I said I would come and speak to them after the game because I want to understand it, I want to understand what they're seeing. Then I can accept a decision that is there. When that decides a game, it's frustrating, because it's not within the laws of the game." Ho admitted WSL referees have "a hard enough job" to do, but believes the standards have "got worse than last year". There is currently no use of video assistant referees (VAR) or goalline technology in the WSL, while not all officials are full-time. Earlier this month, the Guardian reported the wait for full-time WSL referees was set to continue until 2029 despite a recent funding boost. Asked how standards could improve, Ho added: "They need more support and more full-time [referees]. "I understand there is probably a rule where they can't do more than one game on a weekend and that's nothing against any of the referees, but they had an elite referee [Lisa Benn] on the side the pitch. For a big game, put them in the middle. "I think that's where they need more support, more training, because when you look at most decisions that are going on, there's a lot of controversy in a lot of games. "We got two bookings in the first half but we were being dragged back by the shirt by Arsenal players and didn't get nothing. That's probably the frustrating part." BBC Sport has contacted WSL Football for a response. item.description: IMAGO / Every Second Media Chelsea v Leeds United, Carabao Cup Manager Xabi Alonso of Chelsea arrives to the stadium before the Chelsea v Leeds United Carabao Cup 3rd Round match at Stamford Bridge, London, England on 9 September 2026 Cre… | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Alex Richards, LWOF Editor The squad’s dropped for Chelsea vs Tottenham Hotspur with one big absentee that shocked Blue fans. The news of a Joao Pedro injury has caused some concern after the Brazilian started hot with five goals and three assists since the start of the season. Manager Xabi Alonso spoke to the media before the London derby and provided some more details on the nature of the issue impacting the attacker. More Details on Joao Pedro Injury via Xabi Alonso Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images What The Manager Had to Say The Spaniard specified some details, noting that Pedro pulled up on Friday during training. The player felt an issue and has to undergo some testing. The worrying statement is that the player is still to undergo tests to determine “how big” the injury is. Tests and uncertainty are never fun for fans to deal with as it is easy to assume the worst for any player who has dealt with issues in the past. For now, the manager will have to focus on finding a solution for his team in the absence of one of his star attackers. The Last Word The Brazilian striker has been dealing with injuries already in this term, he missed the loss to Brentford just before the international break. His hot start to the season as well as the sale of Nicolas Jackson, leaves the squad without a similar striking profile. Danny Welbeck has been decent since joining but he is a totally different profile at his age. Blues fans will be hoping that this is just a temporary problem and that Pedro will be back soon lest they continue to see some experimentation in the effective front three with Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers. item.title: Jacob Misiorowski Breaks Two Aroldis Chapman Records In Game 1 Of World Series
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Jacob Misiorowski The Milwaukee Brewers won Game 1 of the World Series behind five strong innings from Jacob Misiorowski. He had only three strikeouts and has not been as dominant in the postseason as he was in the regular season. However, against a very tough Tampa Bay Rays lineup, he conceded just one run. As always, the velocity was noteworthy from Misiorowski. His first pitch of the game clocked in at 103.5 mph, breaking Aroldis Chapman's record for the fastest pitch thrown in a World Series game. Chapman held the record with a 103.2 mph pitch in Game 2 of the 2016 World Series. However, that was not the only record Misiorowski snatched from the current Boston Red Sox closer. Unai Emery's side continued their turnaround in form after a slow start to the campaign and picked up a fourth straight win across all competitions, and their first league victory at home this season. Manchester City do not enjoy visiting Villa Park and have now lost their last four league games there, while Enzo Maresca saw his 100% league start as City boss vanish. Another tough afternoon in the west Midlands started when Marc Guehi's mistake allowed Jackson to give Villa an early lead. Villa had keeper Zion Suzuki to thank for making several vital saves, and Iliman Ndiaye crashed an effort off the post as Villa held strong to take the lead into the break. Erling Haaland grabbed his ninth league goal of the season to get City level but Jackson buried his second of the afternoon - his fourth of the season - on the hour mark to hand Villa the points. Arsenal wipe out gap to City Centre-back partners Ezri Konsa and Gabriel celebrated personal milestones as Arsenal beat Everton 2-0 to move level on points with City. England defender Konsa scrambled home from a corner in the seventh minute at the Emirates Stadium to claim his first goal for the club since arriving from Aston Villa in the summer. Gabriel sealed victory with a second-half header on his 200th Premier League appearance, ensuring the Gunners took full advantage of City's 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa in Saturday's early kick-off. Victory for Mikel Arteta's reigning champions was a seventh from eight top-flight fixtures this season and an 11th from 13 games in all competitions. Everton had opportunities to spring a surprise, with Thierno Barry and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall wasting their best openings before they slipped to a second-successive defeat. item.title: Maresca backs Man City defender after first Premier League defeat of season
item.description: Maresca backs Man City defender after first Premier League defeat of season Enzo Maresca insists he has no concerns over Marc Guehi after substituting the defender during Manchester City’s 2-1 defeat to Aston Villa. Guehi was taken off at the break having made an error for Villa’s opener and also been booked in the first half. But Maresca has backed the defender and insists he is not concerned by his performance. “It’s just a technical decision, like it happens in all the games that the manager decides to make a change,” Maresca said. “I’m not worried about Marc at all. I know that he is playing every minute since the season started with us and with the international team. “It’s not easy but the change was also because he had a yellow card, and the way we want to be aggressive sometimes, to have one yellow card can be dangerous. “But I’m not worried at all.” Maresca also felt City deserved more from the game at Villa Park. “I think we deserved more from the game, for the amount of chances that we created and for the chances that we conceded,” he said.

item.title: 1 assist, 2 key passes: Jayce Fitzgerald continues to be Man United’s shining light on loan
item.description: 1 assist, 2 key passes: Jayce Fitzgerald continues to be Man United’s shining light on loan Manchester United had only one player involved in loan action this Saturday afternoon. Loan situation Injuries to Jack Moorhouse and Dan Gore have derailed their loan progress. Sekou Kone and Jacob Devaney were both gaining substantial minutes, but direct red cards have seen them suspended recently. Chido Obi has also seen his game time limited to minutes off the bench, and Altay Bayindir is yet to play for Celta Vigo. Therefore, alongside Andre Onana, Jayce Fitzgerald has been the United loanee who has been involved the most for his loan side. Match vs Shrewsbury Town Fitzgerald played the entire match as his Rotherham United side played out an entertaining 3-3 draw with Shrewsbury Town. The game was also noteworthy for United fans as former player Brandon Williams came off the bench for the final 30 minutes of the game. Fitzgerald’s biggest contribution was an assist to Tom Bradshaw as the Millers equalised 2-2 despite playing with a man less. The 19-year-old’s ball was described as “perfect” by Rotherham’s social media as he continues to impress for the League Two side. The United midfielder made two key passes in the match and completed two crosses for the home side. He also made 74% of his passes and had one shot on goal. Fitzgerald could not complete any dribbles or tackles for his side. The United man made two clearances, but he could not win any duels as he was outmuscled in the centre of the park. He will next be in action away to Swindon Town on Halloween afternoon. Jayce Fitzgerald stats vs Shrewsbury Town Feature image Matt McNulty via Getty Images online polls

item.title: Bayern Munich without three key players for Freiburg clash
item.description: Bayern Munich without three key players for Freiburg clash Bayern Munich will be looking to maintain their unbeaten start to the Bundesliga season when they travel to Europa-Park Stadion to face Freiburg. The Bavarian giants sit top of the Bundesliga table with 14 points from six games and have already scored 22 goals. Freiburg have impressed this season, too, sitting third in the table with 13 points after picking up four wins. Bayern Munich injury news vs Freiburg (Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images) Bayern are dealing with several injury and fitness concerns ahead of the match. Christian Falk has informed CFBayern Insider that Manuel Neuer will not be available for Bayern’s away Bundesliga fixture against Freiburg. The Bayern skipper will sit out the match due to persistent tendon irritation in his foot. Falk said: “His foot appears to remain a weak point for Manuel Neuer; we recall that he previously suffered a serious foot injury. “This makes it all the more important to have a successor like Jonas Urbig already within the club’s ranks. We have heard that he was promised 25 competitive appearances this season as part of a transition period—a number that could now even increase, given the issues with Neuer’s foot.” The Bavarian giants could also be without Vincent Kompany in the dugout for this game. Kompany required medical attention on Friday after collapsing during a training session involving Bayern’s reserve team. The first-team head coach had been observing the second team’s session when the incident occurred. Kompany is currently undergoing a thorough examination in hospital and will remain under medical care, with his coaching staff overseeing all training and match-related operations in the meantime. Luis Diaz also picked up an injury during Bayern’s 2-2 draw against Arsenal in the Champions League and is expected to be out for at least a few weeks. Bayern will also be without their influential midfielder Joshua Kimmich, who has been granted compassionate leave following the death of his father. Kimmich has yet to return to Bayern training. Bayern Munich: Tough game vs Freiburg (Photo by Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images) Jonas Urbig is a highly talented goalkeeper, and Bayern have full confidence in his abilities, believing he has the potential to become the club’s first-choice goalkeeper in the future. Urbig is likely to start in goal, while Tom Bischof should feature in midfield alongside Aleksandar Pavlovic. Bayern have drawn two away games this season, and Freiburg could pose a stern test given their impressive form.

item.title: Jaguars get Brian Thomas Jr. trade update from NFL execs that's not a surprise
item.description: Jaguars get Brian Thomas Jr. trade update from NFL execs that's not a surprise originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Jacksonville Jaguars are heading into their Week 7 bye with a lot of eyes on them. While the Jaguars lead the AFC South, the attention is not due to how good the team is, but rather to a potential trade. After not playing a single snap in the second-half of Week 6, Brian Thomas Jr., the Jaguars first-round wide receiver from the 2024 NFL Draft, seems like a very reasonable trade candidate. Jacksonville hasn't made their plans known, but ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Saturday morning that multiple NFL executives believe the Jaguars will "seriously consider" a trade of Thomas, which shouldn't come as a surprise at all. Jaguars reportedly will 'seriously consider' trading Brian Thomas Jr. "Multiple league execs believe Jacksonville will seriously consider trading Brian Thomas Jr. at the deadline now that his role has decreased," Fowler reports. This is not a surprise at all for the Jaguars, as all of the signs this season, and even over the NFL offseason, pointed to Thomas being a trade chip. Parker Washington has completely broken out as a No. 1 wide receiver, and Jakobi Meyers is a very strong No. 2 option in Liam Coen's offense. Josh Cameron has played himself into a bigger role, and with Travis Hunter able to get onto the field and make a meaningful impact as a WR, the Jaguars don't really have a need for Thomas. MORE : Travis Hunter made NFL history, but the Jaguars still left London with a loss While trading him might require the team to explore some WR depth options, the potential return for a trade of the first-rounder might be appealing enough to move the needle for Jacksonville. Will they actually trade him? It's not impossible, especially if there's a team willing to take a chance on Thomas as a long-term option. The Las Vegas Raiders make a ton of sense, as do a team like the New York Giants . This is a trade situation to closely monitor, as all indications are that a deal is very much under consideration for the Jaguars. It's not locked in like the Marvin Harrison Jr. trade was, but Thomas is a name to keep a very close eye on going forward this year. item.title: Steelers Give Aaron Rodgers Another Familiar Option
item.description: receiver Brandon Smith at training camp on Aug. 7, 2026. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now For the third week in a row, the Pittsburgh Steelers have elevated Brandon Smith from the practice squad. Smith , who has a prior rapport with quarterback Aaron Rodgers, has played 57 offensive snaps this season, including 41 during last Sunday’s win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The Steelers had signed Smith to a reserve/future contract at the end of last season. He had stints with the Jets during the 2024 and 2025 seasons, spending time on both the active roster and practice squad. Smith has also made stops with the New England Patriots, Dallas Cowboys and Arizona Cardinals. “He cooked a lot of guys in the (practice) squad. I mean, every single day, B-Smith was making plays,” Rodgers said earlier this month of Smith’s time with the Jets. “I think he really transformed his body too. Lost a little bit of weight, got a little faster. He’s a smart guy. He’s quiet, goes about his business, very professional. Very, very good in practice. Shows a lot of things. “I have a lot of trust in him. An organization facing tight end injuries might find his receiving experience valuable, especially if it requires someone who can operate in multiple formations. While moving Smith would sacrifice useful depth, the potential return could be worth considering while he still has a recognizable résumé and an expiring contract. item.title: Three things we learnt from Bundesliga Matchday 7 – Antonio Nusa, Werder Bremen are fun and Said El Mala
item.description: Three things we learnt from Bundesliga Matchday 7 – Antonio Nusa, Werder Bremen are fun and Said El Mala Borussia Mönchengladbach began Bundesliga Matchday 7 with a 3-2 win against Stuttgart to avoid setting an all-time Bundesliga record for the worst start ever. Saturday afternoon was a day for the mid-table teams, with Augsburg playing Union Berlin, Köln hosting Schalke, Mainz facing Werder Bremen, Paderborn against Hamburg and RB Leipzig versus Elversberg. Here are the three things we learnt: Antonio Nusa is RB Leipzig’s most important player: In the summer, Nusa was an important player for Norway’s run to the quarter-finals of the World Cup, and he has seemingly carried on this form into this season. In seven Bundesliga games, the winger has three goals and five assists, which makes him the RB Leipzig player with the most goal involvements in the league, ahead of Christopher Nkunku. With the Frenchman out for the game against Elversberg, Nusa stepped up again, providing two assists as Martin Demichelis’ side beat newly promoted Elversberg 4-0 at home. If Nusa continues this form, he will likely be Leipzig’s next big sale in the summer. However, in his two full seasons at the Red Bull Arena, the 21-year-old’s main problem has been staying injury-free, as he has hit similar veins of form only for injury to derail him, and he cannot find the same form when he returns. Werder Bremen are a fun team: After they struggled in the Bundesliga last season, Werder Bremen have turned themselves into a team where their games may be must-watch, mainly due to the goals involved. In their past five games, they’ve had three comebacks and scored five, four, four, and today five goals after beating Mainz 3-2. Niclas Füllkrug again pitched in with a double from the penalty spot before Anthony Caci made it 2-1 just before the break. In the second half, Ludovic Reis made it 3-1, but two minutes later Jae-Sung Lee made it 3-2, and unlike their opponents in the past few weeks, Bremen were able to hold on to secure the three points and move into sixth. Obviously, this is entirely unsustainable, and if Bremen are going to be outsiders for a European spot this season, they need to shore up their defence. Said El Mala should have been sent off: After a transfer saga in the summer, and what seemed like a hot start to the season, Said El Mala’s Bundesliga campaign has stalled in recent weeks. The 20-year-old has largely been ineffective for Köln, and that was shown today in their 0-0 draw with Schalke. However, an argument can be made that El Mala shouldn’t have even been on the pitch for the 80 minutes he was. There was a moment just before half-time where El Mala pushed Schalke’s Soufian El-Faouzi into Robin Gosens as both were challenging for an aerial ball. This resulted in the pair colliding head-on and ultimately both being substituted off. El Mala was punished in no way at all, not even a yellow card. GGFN | Jack Meenan

item.title: Namibia beat Ireland after Erasmus' 156 not out
item.description: Gerhard Erasmus previous highest ODI score had been 125 [Getty Images] Second one-day international, Windhoek Namibia 321-6 (50 overs): Erasmus 156* (125), Frylinck 76 (90); Hoey 3-53 Ireland 290 (47.3 overs): Stirling 77 (71); Brassell 4-52 Namibia win by 31 runs, five-game series tied 1-1 Scorecard An unbeaten 156 from Gerhard Erasmus saw Namibia level their five-game one-day international series against Ireland at one win apiece. The Namibia captain twice took the game away from the tourists in Windhoek as his side won by 31 runs. First, a career-best effort with the bat helped set an imposing total of 32. The 31-year-old then took the final two wickets of the game as Ireland's tail threatened to make an unlikely chase. Ireland captain Paul Stirling won the toss and, having put the hosts into bat, saw his bowling attack struggle, especially in the death overs. Again without leading seamer Mark Adair, Byron McDonough took a wicket with the first ball of his spell but ended up with 1-71. Curtis Campher's 10 innings were also costly as he finished with 1-74. Spinner Gavin Hoey was the pick of the bunch as he matched his trio of wickets from Wednesday's victory, this time with figures of 3-53. As they set about chasing 322, Stirling's uptick in form continued with a second half-century of the series, this time with a knock of 77 from 71 deliveries. His wicket, leg before off the bowling of Jack Brassell, however ended a spell where three batters were dismissed for the addition of just six runs. Brassell was the pick of Namibia bowlers, accounting for not only Stirling but also Lorcan Tucker, George Dockrell and Curtis Campher as he finished with 4-52. A ninth-wicket stand of 58 from Hoey and Jai Moondra briefly brought Ireland within sight, but when the latter was out for 20, caught and bowled by Erasmus, hopes were quickly dashed. The series resumes on Tuesday in Windhoek as Ireland continue their preparations for next year's World Cup qualifiers.

item.description: Millennium remained unbeaten, defeating Canyon View, 6-3, in overtime on Friday, Oct. 23, in a game that was scoreless after four quarters. Austin Honsa, who got Canyon View on the board in overtime. Kadin Johnson, who caught the winning TD pass for Millennium. A late double by Yaqeen Ahmed sealed victory for the South Africans, with the Llanelli-based side having to be content with a try bonus when they had given themselves a shot at a famous win. While the UK was battered by Storm Boelo and south west Wales was still suffering the effects of Storm Austen, perfect conditions for running rugby in Cape Town led to a mad encounter in which both sides traded blows and line breaks. Stormers led 33-14 at half-time and had their try bonus point secure through efforts by Zachary Porthen, Hasseim Pead, Ntuthuko Mchunu, Seabelo Senatla and Deon Fourie. More efforts followed by Olly Reid and Ahmed, but Scarlets showed fighting spirit and attacking flair. Wales centre Roberts went over three times along with Ioan Jones, Josh Macleod and Macs Page, who was helped from the field after a heavy head injury. Tandy on copping flak and his tough Wales calls Scarlets wing Page tipped for huge Wales future Scarlets, who have never beaten Stormers, scrapped their way to 40-40 in the final quarter and seemed to be in the ascendancy, but failed to make it a hat-trick of wins after successes against Benetton and Newcastle in Llanelli. They now finish the first block of the season with an equally daunting fixture against Bulls in Pretoria on Saturday, 31 October (15:00 GMT). Nigel Davies' side will need to drastically improve their defence and set-piece if they are to stand a chance of upsetting the odds with their expansive approach at Loftus Versfeld. Scarlets were chasing the game from early on after John Dobson's side struck twice when hooker John McKee was yellow-carded for cynically killing the ball in the 11th minute. Tight-head prop Porthen went over from a cunning line-out move followed by a much more dashing second, scrum-half Pead crossing from a sensational Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu offload behind his back. Tight-head prop Porthen went over from a cunning line-out move followed by a much more dashing second, scrum-half Pead crossing from a sensational Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu offload behind his back. The 14-man Scarlets responded well with Roberts, who missed out on Wales' Nations Championship squad, put over down the right by wing Jones. But that was cancelled out by rampaging loose-head Ntuthuko Mchunu powering over from loose line-out ball. After providing an assist for the first, Jones finished magnificently down the right for Scarlets' second, but once again Stormers hit straight back. Wing Senatla and hooker Fourie scored either side of a second Jones effort being chalked off for a forward pass for a commanding 33-14 lead. Tonga forward Sam Lousi signed for Scarlets in 2019 [Huw Evans Picture Agency] It seemed that Scarlets were already playing for a consolation bonus in a heavy loss, yet it was game on thanks to a pair of quickfire tries after the restart. A searing break by full-back Ioan Nicholas led to in-form wing Page going over and then Roberts intercepted for the four-try bonus. Page was then helped from the field with an oxygen mask after hitting his head heavily on the ground as he attempted to score. Stormers turned to their tight game to regain control, earning penalties to march down the field for prop Reid to score. Scarlets would not go away and it was a seven-point game on the hour after captain Macleod profited from neat handling. They had the momentum and it was level at 40-40 with quarter of an hour to go when Roberts went through midfield for his hat-trick. With Stormers hindered by the absence of a specialist hooker, which led to uncontested scrums, Scarlets scented a famous win. Yet the hosts got their noses back in front in the 73rd minute when Ahmed was worked under the posts and he took away one of Scarlets' bonuses with a late breakaway. item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Post-Ferguson worn-out horror show continues at Manchester United
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! We’re in the midst of what the kids call “spooky season” – or, for our fellow fusty old-timers out there, “autumn”. If you’ve been cosying up with a few horror flicks this month, you’ll know nothing good can come from hanging around a lake at this time of year. And so it proved for Manchester United, who endured an early Halloween nightmare on the banks of Lake Como that may have driven a stake through the Michael Carrick era. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
